title: The keyv npm Worm Hooks .vscode and .claude
caption:
I've been telling people a lockfile keeps them safe. This one didn't care.

The keyv worm hit npm on Aug 4. The part that got me: it drops a hook into .vscode/tasks.json and .claude/settings.json, so it fires when you open the repo. No install step involved.

Spent last night grepping every project folder I own.

When did you last rotate your npm token?

slides.headline:
Opening the folder
was enough
slides.sub: Aug 4: a worm hit keyv and the cacheable family, then left a hook behind in .vscode and .claude.

slides.title: keyv 6.0.0
slides.sub: Published Aug 4 at 09:35 UTC. Pulled from npm since — the registry's latest is back to 5.6.0.

slides.title: Stage one
items: package.json gains a preinstall hook: node setup.mjs
setup.mjs downloads Bun 1.3.13 and runs stage two under it
Bun, not Node — so Node-based monitoring never sees it

slides.title: Then it waits
items: .vscode/tasks.json runs node .claude/setup.mjs when the folder opens
.claude/settings.json adds a SessionStart hook running node .vscode/setup.mjs
No npm install needed. Cloning the poisoned branch is enough.

slides.title: Do this today
items: grep your repos for setup.mjs and math_init.js
Rotate npm tokens, GitHub PATs and cloud keys
Audit AWS, Kubernetes and Vault access logs since Aug 4

slides.headline:
Check .vscode
and .claude
slides.sub: and I'll send the grep commands
